steps.message:
Item 054 on the verification register for Birchwood Village Expansion, Package A has to close before 07/20/2026. It covers the slab-on-grade fill compaction testing Vantree ran on 07/08/2026 and their Field Density Report SF-26-0708, issued the next day.

Work those results against Specification Section 31 20 00, Earth Moving, and give me an acceptance determination. State the acceptance basis you are using, the limits it produces, and what in the record establishes that basis for this fill.

Cover the testing as well as the results. I want to know whether what was done and recorded is enough to support the determination under that section, and what has to be in hand before anything is built on this fill.

Two files are attached: Fill_Placement_Records_BlockA_SlabOnGrade.xlsx, the Contractor's placement log for this fill, and Thelbridge_Materials_Acceptance_Record_TEMPLATE.docx, our house format for a materials acceptance record. Use the template and save the finished record as /filesystem/Thelbridge_Materials_Acceptance_Fill_Compaction_2026-0708.docx.
I'll start by exploring the filesystem to see what's available.

SECTION 31 20 00
                                         EARTH MOVING

                        Birchwood Village Expansion Program — Package A
                                      Thornbury State University

          Structural Engineer of Record: Calloway Braddock Structural Engineers, LLC
                            812 East Broad Street, Columbus, OH 43205

     Revision: Rev.3 | Issue Date: 03/06/2026 | Supersedes: Rev.2 (issued 11/14/2025)



PART 1    GENERAL

   1.1 SUMMARY
   A. Section Includes:
         1. Excavation, subgrade preparation, and grading for building foundations, mat foundations,
            pile caps, footings, and slabs-on-grade within the Package A limits of work.
         2.    Placement, moisture-conditioning, and compaction of engineered structural fill under
              building foundations and slabs-on-grade.
         3. Backfill against foundation walls and around subsurface structures.
         4. Field quality control by the Owner's independent testing laboratory.
   B. Related Sections:
         1.    Section 31 23 33 — Trenching and Backfilling for utility trenches within the building
              envelope.
         2. Section 31 50 00 — Excavation Support and Protection for delegated shoring design.
         3. Section 03 30 00 — Cast-in-Place Concrete for placement of concrete against completed
            subgrade.

   1.2 REFERENCES
   A.    Referenced Standards. The following standards are incorporated by reference to the extent
         cited herein. The latest edition in effect at the date of Contract award shall govern.
         1.   ASTM D698 — Standard Test Methods for Laboratory Compaction Characteristics of
              Soil Using Standard Effort (Standard Proctor). Cited for historical borrow characterization
              only; not the acceptance basis for Package A structural fill.
         2.   ASTM D1557 — Standard Test Methods for Laboratory Compaction Characteristics of
              Soil Using Modified Effort (Modified Proctor). Governing laboratory reference for
              Package A structural fill.
         3. ASTM D6938 — Standard Test Methods for In-Place Density and Water Content of Soil
            and Soil-Aggregate by Nuclear Methods (Shallow Depth). Governing field density test
            method.
         4.     ASTM D2216 — Standard Test Methods for Laboratory Determination of Water
              (Moisture) Content of Soil and Rock by Mass. Referee method for moisture content




                                         31 20 00 - Page 1 of 6
                                             Earth Moving
           when the nuclear gauge reading is disputed.
     5. ASTM D2937 — Standard Test Method for Density of Soil in Place by the Drive-Cylinder
        Method. Alternate field density method where permitted in writing by the Structural
        Engineer of Record.

1.3 DEFINITIONS
A.   Structural Fill: Imported or on-site engineered soil placed and compacted in controlled lifts
     beneath building foundations, mat foundations, pile caps, footings, or slabs-on-grade, and
     meeting the material, gradation, and compaction requirements of this Section.
B. Common Fill: Non-structural earth used only for site grading outside the building envelope.
C.    Lift: A single layer of loose fill placed in preparation for compaction, not exceeding the
     maximum loose lift thickness specified in Part 3.
D.    Test Location: A single field-density test point at which both dry density and moisture
     content are measured for compliance evaluation.
E.    Placed Material: The specific soil material actually placed in the field at the test location,
     whose laboratory maximum dry density and optimum moisture content have been established
     by ASTM D1557 Method C laboratory testing prior to placement, as required by Article 2.1.

1.4 QUALITY ASSURANCE
A. Testing Laboratory. Field and laboratory testing under this Section shall be performed by the
   Owner's independent construction materials testing laboratory (the “Laboratory”), contracted
   directly to the Owner. The Contractor shall coordinate access, sampling opportunity, and
   lift-by-lift notification with the Laboratory.
B.    Personnel. Nuclear-gauge operators shall hold current radiation safety training and shall be
     documented as competent in ASTM D6938 direct-transmission procedures. Nuclear gauges
     shall be calibrated within the manufacturer's stated interval and standard-count checked at
     the start of each testing day.
C.     Placed-Material Correspondence. The laboratory maximum dry density and optimum
     moisture content used as the acceptance denominators for any test location shall be those
     determined by ASTM D1557 Method C on the material actually placed at that location. Where
     the placed material differs materially from the previously characterized borrow, a new ASTM
     D1557 Method C test shall be performed on the new material before further fill placement is
     accepted.

1.5 SUBMITTALS
A. Prior to structural fill placement, submit for review:
     1.    Source identification for each proposed borrow, including gradation (sieve analysis),
          Atterberg limits, and USCS classification.
     2.   Laboratory report of maximum dry density and optimum moisture content per ASTM
          D1557 Method C for each proposed source material.
     3.    Placement and compaction plan identifying lift thickness, compaction equipment, and
          passes.
B. During placement, submit daily:




                                     31 20 00 - Page 2 of 6
                                         Earth Moving
          1. Field density reports per ASTM D6938 identifying test location, lift number, elevation, dry
            density, moisture content, the ASTM D1557 Method C laboratory maximum dry density
            and optimum moisture content used as denominators, percent compaction, and moisture
            deviation from optimum.

   1.6 SEQUENCING
   A.     No structural fill shall be placed until the underlying subgrade has been proof-rolled in the
         presence of the Laboratory and accepted in writing by the Owner's Representative Engineer.
   B.     No fill placement shall proceed on any lift until the preceding lift has been tested and
         accepted per Article 3.4.

PART 2    PRODUCTS

   2.1 STRUCTURAL FILL
   A.     Material. Well-graded granular fill classified SM or SW-SM, laboratory-tested per ASTM
         D1557 Method C (modified Proctor) prior to placement.
   B.     Gradation. Structural fill shall meet the following gradation, with no more than 12% passing
         the No. 200 sieve and a plasticity index not exceeding 6.
   C.     Deleterious Material. Structural fill shall be free of organic material, frozen soil, debris, and
         particles greater than 3 inches in largest dimension.
   D.    Laboratory Characterization. For each source and for each material change, the Laboratory
         shall determine the maximum dry density and optimum moisture content by ASTM D1557
         Method C prior to placement. The resulting laboratory values are the denominators against
         which the acceptance criteria of Article 3.4.B are evaluated.

   2.2 COMMON FILL
   A. Common fill placed outside the building envelope shall be free of organic material, debris, and
      frozen soil, but is not subject to the acceptance criteria of Article 3.4.B.

   2.3 CAPILLARY BREAK / DRAINAGE COURSE
   A. Clean, open-graded crushed stone, 3/4 in nominal, less than 2% passing the No. 200 sieve,
      placed as shown on the Drawings beneath slabs-on-grade.

PART 3    EXECUTION

   3.1 EXAMINATION
   A.     Examine subgrade prior to fill placement. Do not proceed with fill placement over subgrade
         that is soft, yielding under proof roll, frozen, or otherwise unsuitable. Notify the Owner's
         Representative Engineer in writing of any unsuitable subgrade condition.

   3.2 SUBGRADE PREPARATION
   A. Strip topsoil, organic material, and any existing uncontrolled fill from beneath the footprint of
      structural fill.
   B. Proof-roll exposed subgrade with a loaded tandem-axle dump truck or equivalent equipment
      approved in writing by the Owner's Representative Engineer. The Laboratory shall be present




                                          31 20 00 - Page 3 of 6
                                              Earth Moving
      to witness the proof roll.
C.    Undercut and replace yielding areas with structural fill placed and compacted per this
     Section.

3.3 PLACEMENT
A. Place structural fill in horizontal lifts not exceeding 12 inches loose thickness.
B.    Moisture-condition each lift, by wetting or drying and mixing, so that the moisture content at
     the time of compaction is within the range specified in Article 3.4.B.
C.    Compact each lift with equipment sized and operated to achieve the density and moisture
     requirements of Article 3.4.B throughout the full thickness of the lift.
D.     Do not place fill on frozen subgrade or with frozen material. Do not place fill during
     precipitation that raises the placed material's moisture content above the upper limit of Article
     3.4.B.

3.4 COMPACTION
A. Method Statement. The Contractor shall place structural fill in controlled lifts as specified in
   Article 3.3, moisture-conditioning each lift as necessary to bring the material within the
   moisture range required by Article 3.4.B before compaction. Compaction equipment
   (self-propelled vibratory smooth-drum rollers, pad-foot rollers, or plate compactors adjacent to
   structures) shall be operated in a pattern of overlapping passes such that every location
   within a lift receives no fewer than the number of passes established during a
   Contractor-conducted test strip witnessed by the Laboratory and the Owner's Representative
   Engineer. The test strip shall be executed at the start of production placement, using the
   placement source, moisture-conditioning method, lift thickness, and compaction equipment
   intended for production, and shall demonstrate that the criteria of Article 3.4.B are met before
   general production is authorized. Adjacent to walls, columns, and utilities, use hand-operated
   compaction equipment in lifts not exceeding 6 inches loose thickness. Do not operate heavy
   compaction equipment within 3 feet of walls prior to backfill balancing on both sides. Each lift
   shall be tested and accepted per Article 3.4.B before the next lift is placed.
B. Acceptance Criteria.
             Structural fill shall be placed and compacted to a dry density of not less than
             95% of the maximum dry density determined by ASTM D1557 Method C for the
             placed material, AND shall be placed at a moisture content within −1% to +2%
             of the optimum moisture content determined by the same test. Both criteria must
             be satisfied for each test location. Field density shall be measured per ASTM
             D6938 (nuclear gauge, direct-transmission mode) at a frequency of one test per
             5,000 sf per lift.

C.   Failing Tests. Where either the density criterion or the moisture criterion of Article 3.4.B is
     not satisfied at any test location:
     1.    The affected area of the lift shall be reworked (scarified, moisture-conditioned, and
          recompacted, or removed and replaced) at the Contractor's expense.
     2.    Reworked areas shall be retested by the Laboratory. Both the density and moisture
          criteria of Article 3.4.B must be satisfied on the retest before the lift is accepted.




                                     31 20 00 - Page 4 of 6
                                         Earth Moving
      3.   Isolated failing tests may not be averaged with adjacent passing tests to demonstrate
          compliance. Acceptance is evaluated at each test location independently.
D.    Interpretation. No test location shall be accepted on the basis of density alone. No test
     location shall be accepted on the basis of moisture alone. Compliance requires that both the
     density criterion and the moisture criterion of Article 3.4.B be independently satisfied at that
     test location, as measured against the ASTM D1557 Method C laboratory maximum dry
     density and optimum moisture content of the material actually placed at that location.

3.5 BACKFILL AGAINST FOUNDATION WALLS
A. Do not commence backfill against basement or foundation walls until the wall has attained its
   specified 28-day compressive strength, or until permanent lateral support (floor framing) is in
   place and grouted to the wall, whichever occurs first.
B.    Place backfill on both sides of interior walls in balanced lifts not exceeding 12 inches loose
     thickness, differing by no more than one lift side-to-side.
C. Compact backfill to the same acceptance criteria as Article 3.4.B where the backfill supports
   structure or slabs; elsewhere, to 90% of ASTM D1557 Method C maximum dry density.

3.6 SETTLEMENT TOLERANCE
A.   Total and Differential Settlement. Total settlement 1.0 in maximum; differential settlement
     0.5 in maximum over 30 ft.
B.    Application. The tolerances of Paragraph A apply to the completed foundation system as
     constructed on the accepted subgrade and structural fill delivered under this Section. Where
     predicted or monitored settlements exceed the tolerances of Paragraph A, the Structural
     Engineer of Record shall be notified in writing and no additional load shall be applied until a
     written disposition is issued.
C.    Monitoring. Where settlement monitoring points are shown on the Drawings, readings shall
     be taken and transmitted to the Owner's Representative Engineer at the frequency indicated.
     Cumulative settlement approaching either tolerance of Paragraph A shall be reported
     immediately.

3.7 FIELD QUALITY CONTROL
A. Testing frequency for structural fill:
     1. In-place density and moisture: one ASTM D6938 test per 5,000 sf per lift, as required by
        Article 3.4.B, and not fewer than three tests per lift regardless of lift area.
     2.    Laboratory maximum dry density and optimum moisture content: one ASTM D1557
          Method C determination per source, and one additional determination for each material
          change identified by visual classification or gradation.
B.    Reporting. The Laboratory shall issue field density reports within 24 hours of testing. Each
     report shall identify, for each test location, the ASTM D1557 Method C laboratory maximum
     dry density and optimum moisture content used as the denominators, the measured dry
     density, the measured moisture content, the percent compaction, the moisture deviation from
     optimum, and the disposition (accept or reject) against Article 3.4.B.
C.    Non-Conforming Work. Any lift not meeting Article 3.4.B, or any lift for which the ASTM
     D1557 Method C denominators used in reporting do not correspond to the material actually
     placed, shall be reworked as required by Article 3.4.C before any additional lift is placed.



                                      31 20 00 - Page 5 of 6
                                          Earth Moving
       3.8 PROTECTION
      A.     Protect accepted subgrade and completed structural fill from disturbance, softening by
           precipitation, freezing, and construction traffic until covered by permanent construction.
           Rework and retest, at the Contractor's expense, any area disturbed or softened prior to
           permanent cover.


                                     END OF SECTION 31 20 00

X-Reference: Birchwood Village Package A

MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset="utf-8"
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 7bit

Adrian —

With the Level-3 concrete placement on 07/22/2026 approaching and several items still open on the Package A register, I want to confirm the position we agreed at award: no permanent work on Package A proceeds until Thelbridge has issued a written verification. That is the hold-point we set at Notice to Proceed, and it applies equally to the Level-3 pour and to every other operation on the current list.

Please close the current list — the shoring for the August Block B excavation, the pile downdrag question, the mat buoyancy check, Block C long-term settlement, this week's rebar lot and concrete breaks, the slab-on-grade compaction results, the podium deflection check, the basement seepage assessment, and the reinforcement cover on foundation and exterior work — and let me know by 07/20/2026 which are cleared and which are not.

If any item cannot be verified in time, we would rather delay the pour than release non-conforming work. I would appreciate a short written status against each item by end of day 07/20/2026 so that Steven and Gregory have a clean picture before the 07/22/2026 hold-point is either released or moved. If it is easier to walk me through it beforehand, I am available Monday afternoon.

Thank you.

Rachel

(a) Level-2 concrete 28-day cylinder reports issued 07/06/2026 — five sets, results confirm the mix.

3. SITE DESCRIPTION AND GEOLOGIC SETTING

 3.1 Site Location and Topography
 The Package A site is located at 1802 Larchwood Avenue, on the western portion of the Thornbury State
 University main campus in Columbus, Ohio. The site is bounded to the north by Larchwood Avenue, to the east
 by an existing campus surface parking lot, to the south by an unimproved landscaped strip and to the west by an
 existing academic building. The overall Package A footprint is approximately 3.7 acres.
 Existing topography varies substantially across            Ground surface stands at approximately El. 750.0 ft
 across the footprints of Blocks A and C in the northern and eastern portions of           Toward the southwest,
 across the footprint of Block B, ground surface falls to about El. 738.0 ft (a difference of about 12 ft) in what
 appears from historical aerial photography to have been a surface drainage swale draining the pre-development
 ground westward toward a former off-site low area. The transition between the two elevations is gradual across
 a nominal 60 to 80 ft width. Existing ground within Block B is generally covered with a thin (~0.5 to 1 ft)
 mantle of soft organic-rich silty topsoil overlying the SP-SM upper sand; no fill of engineering significance is
 present beneath Block B in its current condition.

 3.2 Regional and Local Geology
 Columbus, Ohio lies within the Till Plains section of the Central Lowland physiographic province. Regional
 surficial geology is dominated by Wisconsinan-age glacial deposits — chiefly clay-rich till, glaciolacustrine silt
 and clay, and outwash sand and gravel — overlying Devonian-age carbonate and shale bedrock. Local
 hydrogeology is characterized by a shallow phreatic surface within the outwash and reworked outwash sands, a
 laterally continuous fine-grained aquitard, and a lower confined aquifer within basal outwash sand and gravel
 above bedrock.
 The subsurface conditions encountered in the Package A borings are consistent with this regional framework: a
 medium-dense reworked outwash sand at the surface, a low-permeability clay of glaciolacustrine origin at
 intermediate depth, and a dense outwash sand and gravel aquifer at depth. Bedrock was not encountered within
 the maximum boring depth of 90 ft (approximately El. 660.0). Blow counts in the SW-GW below El. 720.0
 were consistently in the range N ≥ 50 blows per 6 inches, indicating a very dense sand-and-gravel deposit
 suitable as a pile-bearing stratum.

 3.3 Site History and Prior Use
 Site historical review — including review of Franklin County parcel records, USGS topographic maps (1955
 and later editions), and Thornbury State University campus master planning archives — indicates that the
 Package A parcel was in agricultural use through approximately 1958, was acquired by the University in 1962,
 and has been used for surface parking and landscape maintenance since. No prior structures of consequence, no
 known below-grade utilities (other than a single abandoned 6-inch clay drain traced along the historic swale in
 Block B), and no known industrial fill are present within the footprint. Because there is essentially no prior fill
 of engineering significance, the Block B footprint requires new engineered fill — placed on the natural
 clay-upper-sand contact after removal of the topsoil mantle — to bring the site to design grade.


 4. FIELD EXPLORATION




Kelbrook Geotechnical, Inc. | 1120 Kinnear Road, Columbus, Ohio 43212 | (614) 555-0204                         Page 9
 Kelbrook Project No. KGI-2024-0417                           Birchwood Village Package A — Geotechnical Report — Rev.2



 4.1 Borings B-01 through B-09
 Nine borings, designated B-01 through B-09, were advanced across the Package A footprint under the direct
 field supervision of Kelbrook Geotechnical. Drilling was performed 10/28/2024 through 11/22/2024 by a
 licensed drilling subcontractor using a truck-mounted rotary drill rig, 4¼-inch-ID hollow-stem augers to the top
 of the aquifer, and mud-rotary methods below. Boring locations were selected to provide coverage of each
 block footprint, of the basement mat and of the Block B plant-room excavation area. The nine boring locations
 are summarized in Table 4-1 below.
 Table 4-1 — Boring Location Summary
                                                 Ground          Depth   Total Depth
    Boring   Block / Zone                                                                Instrumentation
                                              Surface El. (ft)    (ft)     El. (ft)

     B-01    Block A (northeast)                       750.1        60          690.1 Shallow standpipe piezometer

     B-02    Block A (southwest)                       749.8        55          694.8 —

     B-03    Block A / Block B transition (podium bay 3)
                                                      745.4         60          685.4 Shallow standpipe piezometer

     B-04    Block B (plant-room area)                 738.2        90          648.2 Deep piezometer (aquifer)

     B-05    Block B (west edge)                       738.5        75          663.5 —

     B-06    Block B (plant-room area)                 738.1        85          653.1 — (Shelby-tube sampling)

                                                    750.0           65          685.0 —

 Borings B-04 and B-06 fall inside the Block B plant-room excavation footprint, as required to characterize
 subgrade conditions and the confined aquifer beneath the plant-room. Borings B-07 and B-08 are adjacent to
 the basement mat perimeter beneath the shared Blocks A/B foundation. Boring B-09 was placed at the
 approximate center of the Block C footprint to characterize spread-footing bearing conditions there.

 4.2 Sampling Methods
 Split-spoon (SPT) samples were taken continuously on 2.5 ft centers from the ground surface to a depth of 15 ft,
 and thereafter on 5 ft centers, using an automatic 140-lb hammer per ASTM D1586. Blow counts (N-values)
 were recorded and are shown in the boring logs (see cross-reference in Section 11).
 Thin-walled (Shelby-tube) undisturbed samples of the CL clay aquitard (per ASTM D1587) were recovered at
 selected depths from Borings B-04, B-06 and B-08 for laboratory consolidation and index testing. Samples
 B-06 U3 and B-08 U2 — the two samples selected for one-dimensional consolidation testing — were recovered
 at nominal El. 729.5 and El. 728.7, respectively (mid-depth of the clay).

 4.3 Groundwater Instrumentation
 Five (5) groundwater monitoring installations were made in five of the nine borings:
      • Shallow standpipe piezometers, 2-inch ID PVC, 10 ft slotted screen set in the upper SP-SM sand,
 adequate factor of safety against base heave at the planned subgrade elevation, throughout the planned
 excavation duration, using the confined piezometric head El. 738.0 and the parameters in this report.




 9.5 Engineered Fill Placement over the Clay
 Bringing the Block B footprint to design grade requires placement of engineered fill of nominal 12 ft thickness
 (from natural ground at El. 738.0 up to design grade at El. 750.0). Because there is no substantial engineered fill
 or naturally overconsolidated material above the clay at Block B, the engineered fill is placed directly on the
 stripped clay surface after topsoil removal only.
 The engineered fill loads the underlying normally-consolidated CL clay as an areal surcharge, and consolidation
 of the clay under the fill surcharge will occur. Under the parameters of Table 5-1, the settlement caused by 12 ft
 of fill placed as a wide, essentially areal surcharge is substantial and will accrue over a period on the order of
 years. The engineering consequences must be reconciled by the design team:
      • If the fill is placed and given time to allow the underlying clay to substantially complete primary
      consolidation before piles are driven and the podium is erected, then the residual downdrag on the piles
      (and the residual differential settlement of any structure bearing at grade) is minimized. This is the
      preferred sequence.



Kelbrook Geotechnical, Inc. | 1120 Kinnear Road, Columbus, Ohio 43212 | (614) 555-0204                        Page 18
 Kelbrook Project No. KGI-2024-0417                          Birchwood Village Package A — Geotechnical Report — Rev.2


      • If the schedule requires piles to be driven, and structural loads to be applied, before the underlying clay
      has substantially consolidated, then the still-developing consolidation of the clay must be treated as
      an added load.      Downdrag load contributions from the still-consolidating clay must be included
      additively in the axial demand on the pile, in accordance with Section 8.3.
 Requirements for the fill material itself — gradation, compaction, moisture window, layer thickness and testing
 frequency — are to be specified in the project structural fill specification (Section 31 20 00) and controlled by
 the independent Laboratory. Compaction is to be to 95 percent of the ASTM D1557 (modified Proctor)
 maximum dry density with a moisture window from −1 percent to +2 percent of the modified Proctor optimum;
 density and moisture must both be satisfied for acceptance.

 9.6 Dewatering, Excavation and Construction Considerations
      • The basement excavation for Blocks A and B, with a subgrade at approximately El. 731.5, is above the
      top of the clay (El. 738.0) and above the confined head (El. 738.0), but it is below the shallow water table
      (El. 742.0). Dewatering to control the shallow water table will be required in the upper sand around the
      basement excavation but will not reduce the confined head in the deep aquifer, and is not by itself a
      mitigation for the plant-room base-heave problem.
      • The confined-aquifer condition and the aquitard behavior of the CL clay must be preserved. Any activity
      that penetrates the clay across the plant-room footprint — including piles, pressure-relief wells, or shoring
      elements — must be sealed at the aquitard elevation so as not to short-circuit the aquitard.
      • Temporary sheeting design is a delegated design and is not scoped in this report; however, the shoring
      designer must be furnished with the confined head El. 738.0, the shallow water table El. 742.0, and the
      strength parameters and unit weights of each stratum for use in the shoring calculations.
      • Dewatering discharge is subject to Ohio EPA NPDES permitting requirements.
      Discharge quality (turbidity, TSS) and discharge quantity (rate, volume) will need to be permitted by the
      Contractor as part of the dewatering plan.


 10. LIMITATIONS
 This report has been prepared exclusively for Thornbury State University and its authorized representatives for
 the specific purpose of geotechnical design and construction of the Birchwood Village Package A project at

 1. Purpose and Scope
 This field observation report documents excavation observations, groundwater monitoring readings and seepage
 observations recorded by Kelbrook Geotechnical field personnel across the Package A footprint over the
 construction period 07/2025 through 05/2026. The observations reported herein are drawn from the writer’s
 daily field notes, from the shallow standpipe and deep piezometer monitoring log maintained under the ongoing
 Package A groundwater monitoring program, and from photographs and sketches taken at the time of
 observation. The report is furnished in support of the Owner’s Representative construction verification file and
 as supplemental record to the Geotechnical Investigation Report Rev.2 (KGI-2024-0417).
 Two distinct field episodes are documented: (a) the Block A basement excavation, opened in the summer of
 2025 to a working subgrade at approximately El. 730.0; and (b) the placement of engineered fill across the
 Block B footprint from 10/06/2025 through 11/02/2025 and the subsequent months of pile installation and
 lift-up to design grade. Groundwater monitoring is continuous across both episodes and is reported in full.

 2. Excavation Observations — Block A Basement
 2.1 Excavation Opening and Progression




Field Observation Report — Excavation and Groundwater — Package A                                             Page 1
 Kelbrook Geotechnical, Inc.                                                                                     Report No. KGI-FO-2026-0528




 The Block A basement excavation was opened in the northeast quadrant of the Package A footprint on
 07/14/2025 and progressed from existing grade El. 750.0 down to a working subgrade at approximately El.
 730.0 (approximately one foot below the design underside of the basement mat at El. 731.5, to accommodate a
 lean-concrete working mat). The excavation was carried out by the Contractor using a mid-size hydraulic
 excavator with side dumping to trucks; sequence proceeded from the east perimeter westward across the Block
 A footprint over the course of approximately three weeks.
 Perimeter shoring — a combination of soldier pile and timber lagging along the northern and eastern faces, and
 open-cut battered slopes along the interior (Block A / Block B transition) — was installed ahead of the cut face.
 Well-point dewatering, executed per the Contractor’s Dewatering and Groundwater Control Plan Rev.1
 dated 06/04/2025, was activated on 07/12/2025, two days before the first cut, and remained in operation
 continuously through mat placement on 01/12/2026 and thereafter to protect the wall pour sequence.

 2.2 Side Conditions Observed in the Cut Face
 Exposed cut faces along the Block A perimeter revealed the following, consistent with the strata described in
 Section 6 of the reference report:
   •    From existing grade El. 750.0 down to approximately El. 746.0: approximately 4 ft of loose topsoil,
        root-mat and reworked surface fill of engineering significance limited to the upper 0.5 to 1 ft, transitioning
        downward into weathered upper sand. This layer was over-excavated and hauled off-site as unsuitable for
        structural fill re-use.
   •    From approximately El. 746.0 down to El. 738.0: the SP-SM upper sand — medium-dense, moist above
        the water table and saturated below it, with a modest silt content and no interbedded fine-grained seams.
        Cut face stability in the sand above the water table was satisfactory at 1H:1V; below the water table (once
        dewatered) the face was cut vertically against the shoring without slumping.
   •    From El. 738.0 down to the working subgrade at El. 730.0: the top of the CL clay aquitard, exposed as
        a stiff, medium-plasticity lean clay of grey-brown colour. The top of the clay at El. 738.0 was consistent
        within ± 0.5 ft across the Block A footprint. The clay retained a vertical or near-vertical face for the
        excavation duration without noticeable creep or heave; subgrade compaction footprint (proof-rolling)
        produced no rutting or pumping under the loaded haul truck used for the check.
 The transition from Stratum 1 (upper sand) to Stratum 2 (clay) at El. 738.0 was sharp and well-defined in the cut
 face and matched the elevation logged in Borings B-01, B-02, B-07 and B-09 within a few tenths of a foot.

 2.3 Working Subgrade Condition
 Subgrade at El. 730.0 was inspected on 08/06/2025 in the presence of the Contractor’s Superintendent (Mr.
 Marcus Whitfield) and the Owner’s Representative (Mr. Adrian Vance      ). Subgrade was found to be firm,
 uniform, free of standing water within the dewatered footprint, and suitable to receive the lean-concrete
 working mat and subsequently the reinforced mat foundation. No soft spots, disturbed zones or unsuitable
 inclusions were logged. The subgrade approval memorandum was issued separately by Kelbrook on
 08/07/2025.

 3. Groundwater Monitoring — Continuous Record
 Groundwater monitoring under the Package A program continues from the piezometer array installed
 11/22/2024 and reported in the Geotechnical Investigation Report Rev.2. Over the observation period 07/2025
 through 05/2026 an additional eleven monitoring rounds were completed, bringing the total record to eighteen

 rounds since installation. Readings are taken monthly (weekly during active excavation and dewatering).

 3.1 Design Water Table — Upper Sand (Shallow Standpipe Piezometers)
 The design water table in the upper SP-SM sand, established at El. 742.0 in the reference report, is confirmed
 by the extended monitoring record. Readings from the three shallow standpipe piezometers (B-01, B-03, B-09),
 taken across the 07/2025 through 05/2026 observation period at locations outside the Block A dewatered
 footprint, remain in the range El. 741.6 to El. 742.4, with individual monthly means clustered within a few
 tenths of a foot of El. 742.0. No systematic trend, no seasonal excursion beyond that range and no departure
 from the design elevation was recorded.

 3.2 Confined Piezometric Head — Deep Aquifer (Deep Piezometers)
 The confined piezometric head in the deep SW-GW sand-and-gravel aquifer below El. 720.0, established at El.
 738.0 in the reference report, is likewise confirmed. Readings from the two deep piezometers (B-04 and B-08),
 both screened below El. 720.0 within the Block B footprint, remain in the range El. 737.7 to El. 738.3 across
 the full extended record. The head is stable, without trend, and consistent with the value carried forward from

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Build Thelbridge Materials Acceptance Record for Register Item 054 from the house template."""
import copy
from docx import Document
from docx.shared import Pt, RGBColor
from docx.oxml import OxmlElement
from docx.oxml.ns import qn

TEMPLATE = "/filesystem/Thelbridge_Materials_Acceptance_Record_TEMPLATE.docx"
OUT = "/filesystem/Thelbridge_Materials_Acceptance_Fill_Compaction_2026-0708.docx"
TEXT_W = 9720  # twips (12240 - 2*1260)

doc = Document(TEMPLATE)
P = list(doc.paragraphs)  # P0..P26 per template inspection
assert P[7].text.startswith("1.") and P[10].text.startswith("2.") and P[13].text.startswith("3.")
assert P[16].text.startswith("4.") and P[19].text.startswith("5.") and P[23].text == "Name"


# ----------------------------------------------------------------- helpers
def _rpr(run, size=10, bold=False, italic=False, color=None):
    """Match the template: every run carries explicit Calibri rFonts and size."""
    rPr = run._r.get_or_add_rPr()
    rf = OxmlElement("w:rFonts")
    for a in ("w:ascii", "w:cs", "w:eastAsia", "w:hAnsi"):
        rf.set(qn(a), "Calibri")
    rPr.insert(0, rf)
    run.font.size = Pt(size)
    if bold:
        run.font.bold = True
    if italic:
        run.font.italic = True
    if color:
        run.font.color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string(color)


def _ppr_spacing(p, before=None, after=None, line=None):
    pPr = p._p.get_or_add_pPr()
    sp = pPr.find(qn("w:spacing"))
    if sp is None:
        sp = OxmlElement("w:spacing")
        pPr.append(sp)
    if before is not None:
        sp.set(qn("w:before"), str(before))
    if after is not None:
        sp.set(qn("w:after"), str(after))
    if line is not None:
        sp.set(qn("w:line"), str(line))
        sp.set(qn("w:lineRule"), "auto")


def _ppr_flag(p, tag):
    pPr = p._p.get_or_add_pPr()
    pPr.append(OxmlElement(tag))


def _ppr_ind(p, left=0, hanging=0):
    pPr = p._p.get_or_add_pPr()
    ind = OxmlElement("w:ind")
    ind.set(qn("w:left"), str(left))
    if hanging:
        ind.set(qn("w:hanging"), str(hanging))
    pPr.append(ind)


def add_runs(p, parts, size=10):
    """parts: str or list of (text, dict(bold/italic/color))."""
    if isinstance(parts, str):
        parts = [(parts, {})]
    for text, fmt in parts:
        r = p.add_run(text)
        _rpr(r, size=size, bold=fmt.get("b", False), italic=fmt.get("i", False), color=fmt.get("c"))
    return p


def new_par(parts, size=10, before=0, after=100, keep_next=False, left=0, hanging=0, line=None):
    p = doc.add_paragraph()  # created at end of body, then moved by caller
    _ppr_spacing(p, before=before, after=after, line=line)
    if left or hanging:
        _ppr_ind(p, left, hanging)
    if keep_next:
        _ppr_flag(p, "w:keepNext")
    add_runs(p, parts, size=size)
    return p


def _cell_shade(cell, fill):
    tcPr = cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    shd = OxmlElement("w:shd")
    shd.set(qn("w:val"), "clear")
    shd.set(qn("w:color"), "auto")
    shd.set(qn("w:fill"), fill)
    tcPr.append(shd)


def _cell_width(cell, w):
    tcPr = cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    tcW = tcPr.find(qn("w:tcW"))
    if tcW is None:
        tcW = OxmlElement("w:tcW")
        tcPr.insert(0, tcW)
    tcW.set(qn("w:w"), str(w))
    tcW.set(qn("w:type"), "dxa")


def new_table(rows, widths, size=8.5, header=True, bold_cols=(), center_cols=(), bold_cells=()):
    """rows: list of lists; each cell is str or list of (text, fmt). First row = header if header."""
    assert abs(sum(widths) - TEXT_W) <= 5, (sum(widths), TEXT_W)
    t = doc.add_table(rows=len(rows), cols=len(widths))
    tbl = t._tbl
    tblPr = tbl.tblPr
    # remove any style reference (template defines no table styles)
    for el in tblPr.findall(qn("w:tblStyle")):
        tblPr.remove(el)
    tblW = tblPr.find(qn("w:tblW"))
    if tblW is None:
        tblW = OxmlElement("w:tblW")
        tblPr.append(tblW)
    tblW.set(qn("w:w"), str(TEXT_W))
    tblW.set(qn("w:type"), "dxa")
    layout = OxmlElement("w:tblLayout")
    layout.set(qn("w:type"), "fixed")
    tblPr.append(layout)
    borders = OxmlElement("w:tblBorders")
    for edge in ("top", "left", "bottom", "right", "insideH", "insideV"):
        e = OxmlElement(f"w:{edge}")
        e.set(qn("w:val"), "single")
        e.set(qn("w:sz"), "4")
        e.set(qn("w:space"), "0")
        e.set(qn("w:color"), "7F7F7F")
        borders.append(e)
    tblPr.append(borders)
    mar = OxmlElement("w:tblCellMar")
    for edge, v in (("top", 25), ("left", 70), ("bottom", 25), ("right", 70)):
        e = OxmlElement(f"w:{edge}")
        e.set(qn("w:w"), str(v))
        e.set(qn("w:type"), "dxa")
        mar.append(e)
    tblPr.append(mar)
    # grid
    grid = tbl.tblGrid
    for gc, w in zip(grid.findall(qn("w:gridCol")), widths):
        gc.set(qn("w:w"), str(w))
    for ri, row in enumerate(rows):
        tr = t.rows[ri]._tr
        trPr = tr.get_or_add_trPr()
        trPr.append(OxmlElement("w:cantSplit"))
        if header and ri == 0:
            trPr.append(OxmlElement("w:tblHeader"))
        for ci, val in enumerate(row):
            cell = t.rows[ri].cells[ci]
            _cell_width(cell, widths[ci])
            p = cell.paragraphs[0]
            _ppr_spacing(p, before=0, after=0)
            if ci in center_cols or (header and ri == 0 and ci in center_cols):
                p.alignment = 1
            is_head = header and ri == 0
            if is_head:
                _cell_shade(cell, "D9D9D9")
            parts = val if isinstance(val, list) else [(val, {})]
            for text, fmt in parts:
                f = dict(fmt)
                if is_head or ci in bold_cols or (ri, ci) in bold_cells:
                    f["b"] = True
                r = p.add_run(text)
                _rpr(r, size=size, bold=f.get("b", False), italic=f.get("i", False), color=f.get("c"))
    return t


def place_before(anchor_par, items):
    """Move created paragraphs/tables (in order) to sit immediately before anchor paragraph."""
    for it in items:
        el = it._tbl if hasattr(it, "_tbl") else it._p
        anchor_par._p.addprevious(el)


def remove_par(p):
    p._p.getparent().remove(p._p)


B = {"b": True}
I = {"i": True}

# ----------------------------------------------------------------- header block
def header_value(p, value):
    pPr = p._p.get_or_add_pPr()
    if pPr.find(qn("w:tabs")) is None:
        tabs = OxmlElement("w:tabs")
        tab = OxmlElement("w:tab")
        tab.set(qn("w:val"), "left")
        tab.set(qn("w:pos"), "1200")
        tabs.append(tab)
        # tabs must precede spacing/ind in pPr
        pPr.insert(0, tabs)
    ind = OxmlElement("w:ind")
    ind.set(qn("w:left"), "1200")
    ind.set(qn("w:hanging"), "1200")
    pPr.append(ind)
    if "\t" not in p.text:
        r = p.add_run("\t")
        _rpr(r, size=10)
    r = p.add_run(value)
    _rpr(r, size=10)


header_value(P[3], "Adrian Vance, Project Engineer (Structural/Geotechnical), Owner\u2019s Representative \u2014 Register Owner")
header_value(P[4], "Karen Tarbray, Materials / QA Reviewer")
header_value(P[5], "07/15/2026")
header_value(P[6], "Birchwood Village Expansion Program, Package A \u2014 Verification Register Item 054 \u2014 Block A "

        parts.append((body, {}))

        parts.extend(body)
    return new_par(parts, before=before, after=100, keep_next=keep_next)

    n_fixed = 0

What the record establishes for this fill, and what it does not. The record establishes the criterion — Art.

establish that P04 is the D1557 Method C curve of the material actually placed, which Art. 1.3.E, 1.4.C and

moisture finding in 4.4 holds whichever D1557 Method C curve is ultimately found to govern.

4. FINDINGS
4.1 Wrong reference curve in SF-26-0708. SF-26-0708 computes percent compaction against ASTM D698
Method A, 118.6 pcf at 12.1%, curve of record VMT-2024-0403-P1B (SF-26-0708 p.1 §3). P1B is a standardeffort test on Wexford Ridge Borrow, a Phase 1 off-site source, classified CL-ML with PI 11 and 68% passing
the No. 200 sieve (P1B p.1 §§1–2; p.2 §6; p.3). It is excluded as an acceptance basis by Art. 1.2.A.1 (Spec
p.1), is not Package A material, and describes a soil that would not qualify as structural fill under Art. 2.1.A–B
(Spec p.3). Vantree’s own sealed P04 states that it supersedes any earlier Proctor result for Package A
structural fill (P04 p.3 §7). The reported compactions of 103.6% to 106.3% — in-place densities above the
laboratory maximum — indicate on their face that the reference does not represent the material tested
(SF-26-0708 pp.1–2 §5). The Laboratory’s report and the Contractor’s placement record cite different
reference curves for the same lift (RB-FPR-BA Cover row 24).
4.2 Density-only evaluation; the report does not conform. SF-26-0708 states the requirement as density
only (p.1 §4), reports no moisture deviation from optimum, and gives the disposition “accepted for density”
(p.2 §6). This contravenes Art. 3.4.B and Art. 3.4.D (“No test location shall be accepted on the basis of
density alone”) and the report-content requirements of Art. 1.5.B.1 and 3.7.B (Spec pp.3–5). The “PASS”
entries have no standing under Section 31 20 00. Even against the D698 values the Laboratory used, none of
the four moisture readings lies within a −1%/+2% window (11.1% to 14.1%); the deviations from the D698
optimum are −6.0, −2.3, −1.7 and −6.3 points.
4.3 Results evaluated against P04 (D1557 Method C). Field values are from SF-26-0708 pp.1–2 §5;
denominators from P04 p.3 §7.

10.4% (4.6 points), while the Art. 3.4.B window is 3.0 points wide (SF-26-0708 pp.1–2 §5; Spec p.4). FD-14
and FD-17 can both meet the window only if the optimum lies between 4.1% and 6.8%; FD-15 and FD-16


 only if it lies between 8.4% and 10.8%. The ranges do not overlap, so at least two of the four locations fail the
moisture criterion whatever D1557 Method C optimum the placed material proves to have. The two clusters
(5.8–6.1% and 9.8–10.4%) also indicate non-uniform moisture conditioning across the lift (Art. 3.3.B, Spec
p.4), consistent with the hot-weather surface moisture loss the Contractor’s field engineer recorded on earlier

4.5 FD-15 and FD-16 cannot be accepted. Both meet the two criteria against P04, but P04 is not
established as the curve of the material placed (Art. 1.4.C and 3.4.D, Spec pp.2, 5; Finding 4.6). Their
margins are narrow: FD-16 would fall below 95% if the placed material’s maximum dry density exceeded
about 129.4 pcf (1.0 pcf above P04), and FD-15 if it exceeded 130.0 pcf; at least one of them would fail
moisture if the optimum lay outside 8.4% to 10.8%. Independently, both were reported against D698, which
places the lift under Art. 3.7.C (Spec p.5).
4.6 The placed material has no D1557 Method C characterization. RB-FPR-BA records the source as the
“Stockpile north of Block C - approved for reuse per RFI 079”, hauled by on-site scraper and articulated truck
with “no off-site delivery tickets” (Cover row 23; Notes row 6), yet carries P04 as the governing Proctor “as

steps.message:
The record is saved to `/filesystem/Thelbridge_Materials_Acceptance_Fill_Compaction_2026-0708.docx` (7 pages, house template). **The determination is REJECTED for all four tests (FD-14 to FD-17, Lift 6).**

**Acceptance basis and limits.** The basis is Article 3.4.B, using Vantree's modified Proctor test P04 (ASTM D1557 Method C): maximum dry density 128.4 pcf at 9.2% optimum moisture. That gives two limits, and both must be met at every test location:
- dry density of at least 122.0 pcf;
- moisture content between 8.2% and 11.2%.

The spec also requires at least three tests on this 11,400 sf lift.

**What the record establishes, and what it doesn't.** The criterion itself is solidly established: Articles 3.4.B and 3.4.D, sheet S-201 Rev.4, the geotechnical report, and the EOR's confirmation under register item 027. The P04 values are not established for this fill:
- P04 was tested on Larchwood Pit material.
- The Contractor's placement log says this fill came from the stockpile north of Block C. RFI 079 accepted that stockpile only "subject to gradation retest."
- There is no Proctor test, gradation or source identification on file for the stockpile.

So the P04 limits can support a rejection but not an acceptance.

**Results**
- **SF-26-0708 used the wrong reference.** It used a standard Proctor (D698) on the Phase 1 Wexford Ridge borrow, a silty clay, which Article 1.2.A.1 excludes. It also checked density only. Its "PASS" results carry no weight under the section.
- **Against P04:** FD-14 (6.1%) and FD-17 (5.8%) fail on moisture. FD-15 and FD-16 meet both limits but can't be accepted until the correct reference for the placed material exists.
- **The rejection holds whatever the correct reference turns out to be.** The moisture readings span 5.8% to 10.4%, wider than the 3-point window, so at least two locations fail under any optimum.

**Is the testing enough?** The test method, gauge calibration, test frequency and lift thickness all conform. It is enough to reject but not to accept:
- there is no reference test on the material actually placed;
- moisture was never evaluated;
- the tester left at 11:30 while placement and grading ran until 17:00;
- the gauge operator's qualifications aren't documented.

**Lifts 1–5 should be treated as unverified.** The log cites lift-by-lift density reports FDR-BA-01 to -05, but none is in the record. The Contractor's own daily report for 06/30 and our June progress report both say density testing was only scheduled for 07/08. The test numbering doesn't add up. About 0.4 in of rain fell on the exposed Lift 5 surface, and the log doesn't mention it.

**Before anything is built on this fill:**
- a modified Proctor test, source identification and the gradation retest on the material actually placed;
- full-lift rework of Lift 6, then retesting against both limits with oven-dry moisture checks;
- Lifts 1–5 verified or remediated;
- the proof-roll acceptance memo TPM-26-063 and the test-strip record placed on file;
- SF-26-0708 withdrawn;
- a new record with an ACCEPTED determination.

The full action list is in Section 5 of the record.

**Decisions for you**
- **Signing:** I set it up as from Karen Tarbray to Adrian Vance, following the register assignment. It is unsigned and dated 07/15/2026 (the register's last-updated date); change the date at signing if needed.
- **Closing item 054:** I recommend recording it as Closed-w-Comment with disposition REJECTED, and opening a follow-on item. That closes it by 07/20 while the pad stays on hold.
- **Rework extent:** requiring rework of the whole lift is a judgment call, based on failures at both ends of the pad and Article 3.7.C. The alternative is to let the Contractor mark out the failing area with extra tests.
- **Our own files:** memo TPM-26-063 and letter TPM-25-079 (the RFI 079 response) are Thelbridge documents that weren't in the record I had. Please check whether they exist.
- **Kendrow's 07/14 email:** the record rejects his claim that SF-26-0708 is compliant. Per the register, the Level-3 pour hold-point is not conditioned on item 054.
